item.title: China remains Kyrgyzstan's largest trading partner
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- China has long remained Kyrgyzstan's largest trading partner, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation making steady progress, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday. China-Kyrgyzstan trade reached 11.7 billion U.S. dollars in the first seven months of this year. During the period, China's exports of electric vehicles, lithium batteries and photovoltaic products, known as the "new three," as well as mechanical and electrical products to Kyrgyzstan grew rapidly, ministry spokesperson Huang Ling said at a regular press conference. "Under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, bilateral economic and trade cooperation has advanced steadily in recent years and produced positive results across various fields," Huang said. China is also Kyrgyzstan's largest source of foreign investment, with its direct investment across all sectors in Kyrgyzstan exceeding 2 billion U.S. dollars at the end of July, she said, adding that projects involving major infrastructure, energy, mining, agriculture and green development are progressing smoothly. The two countries are also exploring ways to advance trade and investment liberalization and facilitation between China and Central Asian countries and within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) to promote regional economic cooperation, Huang said. Going forward, China stands ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and continue promoting the high-quality development of bilateral economic and trade cooperation, said Huang. This year marks the 25th anniversary of the SCO. In 2025, China's trade with other SCO members reached 523.5 billion U.S. dollars and accounted for 8 percent of the country's total foreign trade, up from 12.1 billion dollars in 2001, Huang said, adding that China also saw rapid growth in exports of its "new three" products and in cross-border e-commerce exports to other SCO members. Over the past 25 years, China has upheld the Shanghai Spirit and worked with other SCO members to pursue common development and share in its benefits, helping deliver fruitful results in regional economic cooperation, Huang said. China's investment in other SCO members has continued to expand, with its direct investment across all sectors reaching 3.3 billion U.S. dollars in 2025. The investment covered areas including oil and gas, mineral resources, infrastructure, new energy, automobiles and chemicals, said Huang. China has also invested in and built more than 30 economic and trade cooperation zones, helping SCO member states enhance their capacity for industrial development, she added. China will continue implementing the action plan for high-quality development of economic and trade cooperation with SCO member states, observer states and dialogue partners, promote trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, advance trade in services and digital trade, deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, and take regional economic cooperation to a new level, said Huang.

item.title: Chinese premier urges all-out rescue, emergency response efforts after Gyirong mudslide
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 28 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has called for all-out rescue and emergency response efforts following a mudslide that struck the Gyirong border port in Gyirong County of southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Entrusted by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, traveled to Gyirong County on Thursday to guide rescue and emergency response efforts after the disaster. Five people have been confirmed dead and 558 others are missing after the mudslide hit the border port on Wednesday morning, according to regional authorities. Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made instructions on disaster relief and emergency response operations after the mudslide occurred on Wednesday. Li stressed the importance of implementing the instructions, calling for efforts to put the people and their lives above all else and to spare no effort in carrying out rescue and emergency response work. After arriving at the Xigaze airport, Li proceeded directly to the disaster-hit area in Gyirong, where he inspected the damage and met with rescue workers. Li said rescue plans should be formulated in a scientific manner and every possible effort be made to search for those who are still missing. As long as there is a glimmer of hope, every effort should be made, he said. He also called for swift repairs to damaged infrastructure, including roads, communications and power facilities, to restore access for rescue operations as soon as possible. Expressing appreciation to personnel working on the front lines of the rescue effort, Li later visited temporary shelters for affected residents and conveyed Xi's concern and care to them. Li stressed the need to continue dispatching and transporting disaster-relief supplies and ensure the basic living needs of evacuated and relocated residents. At the front-line command center for the Gyirong mudslide disaster response, Li called for strengthening coordination of rescue personnel and equipment, enhancing unified on-site command, and further efforts to fully ascertain the situation of those still missing. He stressed the need to carry out rescue operations in an orderly and effective manner. It is necessary to strengthen monitoring, forecasting and early warning of weather, hydrological and geological conditions in affected and surrounding areas, as well as take solid epidemic prevention and disinfection measures to guard against secondary disasters, he noted. He urged authorities to release information on the disaster and rescue operations in an open and transparent manner. Li also stressed the need to strengthen foreign-related emergency response, communication and coordination, and work with relevant foreign parties to verify the status of missing persons and well handle follow-up matters. Noting that China is still in the midst of flood season and faces a severe and complex situation regarding flood control and typhoon prevention, Li called for maintaining preparedness for extreme and worst-case scenarios. He urged authorities to remain highly vigilant, intensify inspections and risk-removal efforts in key areas and vulnerable locations, and take solid measures against various natural disasters to safeguard people's lives and property and maintain overall social stability.

item.title: Body of senior national political advisor Chen Wu cremated
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 -- The body of Chen Wu, vice chairman of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, was cremated in Beijing on Friday. President Xi Jinping and other senior leaders of the Communist Party of China and the state, including Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng, bid farewell to Chen at the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery on Friday morning. Amid solemn music, they walked slowly toward Chen's body and stood in silent tribute. They then paid their final respects with three bows and shook hands with Chen's family members. Chen died of illness on Aug. 24 in Beijing at the age of 72. Chen was extolled in an obituary as an excellent Party member, a loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding leader in ethnic affairs and economic construction. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi, Han Zheng and Hu Jintao, among others, had either visited Chen when he was in hospital or expressed deep condolences and offered sincere sympathies to his family through various means after his passing.

item.title: Xi extends condolences over mudslide disaster in Nepal
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday sent a message of condolences to Nepali President Ram Chandra Poudel over a mudslide disaster that hit Nepal recently. In his message, Xi noted that a severe mudslide disaster occurred recently at the Gyirong-Rasuwa border crossing between China and Nepal, causing heavy casualties, leaving people missing and resulting in property losses. On behalf of the Chinese government and people, Xi expressed deep condolences to the victims and sincere sympathies to the bereaved families, the injured and people in the disaster-stricken areas. Xi noted that China is making every effort to search for and rescue missing persons, relocate and resettle affected people, provide prompt medical treatment to the injured, minimize casualties and prevent secondary disasters. China and Nepal, Xi said, are connected by mountains and rivers and share a common destiny, adding that China is ready to actively assist Nepal in its rescue efforts and provide support and assistance to the best of its capability. Xi also expressed his belief that both peoples will be able to work together to overcome the disaster and rebuild their homes as soon as possible. On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang sent a message of condolences to Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

item.title: Xi hails historic leap in China-Kyrgyzstan ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday hailed the historic leap in China-Kyrgyzstan ties from a good-neighborly friendship to a strategic partnership and then to a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era. Xi made the remarks in a signed article published in Kyrgyz media outlets ahead of his state visit to the Central Asian country. In the article, Xi urged China and Kyrgyzstan to consolidate good-neighborly friendship, stay committed to mutual benefit and win-win cooperation, carry forward their traditional friendship and uphold multilateralism. Calling on China and Kyrgyzstan to elevate practical cooperation in both quality and scope with high-quality Belt and Road cooperation as the main focus, he urged the two countries to work together to create a new chapter of high-quality development in bilateral relations. Xi also called on China and Kyrgyzstan to firmly oppose hegemonism, unilateralism and bloc confrontation.

item.title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting on Gyirong County mudslide rescue efforts
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Friday chaired a Party leadership meeting to deliberate and make arrangements on rescue and relief efforts after a devastating mudslide hit Gyirong County in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. At the beginning of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Xi, who is also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, and other leaders, including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, observed a moment of silence to mourn the victims of the disaster. A mudslide in Nepal on Wednesday struck the border port of Gyirong, causing heavy casualties and leaving many people missing. Following the disaster, the CPC Central Committee attached great importance to the situation, and Xi immediately issued important instructions on rescue and emergency response efforts. Entrusted by Xi, Premier Li Qiang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, traveled to the disaster-hit area to visit the affected people and rescue and relief personnel, and to supervise rescue and emergency response efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, also went to the site to guide the response. According to the meeting, emergency rescue operations have been carried out swiftly and in an orderly and well-coordinated manner under the strong leadership of the Party Central Committee, with comprehensive efforts underway for the resettlement of affected people and handling of the aftermath. The disaster occurred in a severely cold plateau region with steep valleys, variable weather, many surrounding glaciers and glacial lakes, as well as potential geological hazards, which poses significant challenges to emergency rescue operations. The meeting emphasized that all relevant authorities and departments must take resolute and effective measures for the rescue-related work. Search and rescue plans should be formulated in a scientific manner, and every effort should be made to search for and rescue all missing Chinese and foreign nationals, it stressed. Multi-department joint consultation must be strengthened, monitoring and early warning enhanced, barrier lake and surrounding mountain stability closely tracked, and effective measures taken to strictly prevent secondary disasters, according to the meeting. It also urged enhancing on-site personnel management to ensure safety throughout the rescue process. China will provide emergency aid to the disaster-hit area in Nepal and carry out international rescue cooperation, the meeting said. The meeting called for conducting comprehensive inspections to identify potential risks and hazards, boosting real-time monitoring and early warning, and enhancing the capacity to identify risks arising from disaster chains. It also urged that emergency response mechanisms should be improved, and key rescue forces be strengthened. More rescue and emergency response forces should be deployed to remote and disaster-prone areas, according to the meeting. International cooperation on disaster management in border areas should also be strengthened to jointly enhance emergency management as well as disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, it added. On better coordinating development and security, the meeting emphasized the need to prepare for worst-case and extreme scenarios, bear a strong sense of political responsibility and constant vigilance, and make solid efforts to ensure safety and stability.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.

item.title: China to revise regulations on housing provident fund management
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-18
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree publicizing a decision to revise the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund, which will take effect on Sept. 20, 2026. According to the decision, the scope of the fund's withdrawal and use will be expanded. For those withdrawing from the housing provident fund to pay rent, the eligibility threshold requiring rent to exceed a prescribed proportion of a household's wage income will be removed. Housing provident fund savings can be withdrawn for new purposes under the revised regulations, including renovating the homes the contributors live in and paying property management fees for such homes. The decision also states that the channels for the investment and utilization of the housing provident fund will be appropriately broadened, specifying that housing provident fund management centers are allowed to use the funds to purchase policy-oriented financial bonds. To enhance the efficiency of management services, the decision also underscores efforts to simplify the procedures for employees to apply for housing provident fund withdrawals and to shorten the review period for housing provident fund loan applications. The decision, which strengthens risk prevention and control, stipulates that housing provident fund management centers should establish comprehensive, complete and accurate credit records and incorporate them into the national credit information sharing platform. Amid efforts to expand the coverage of the system, the decision clarifies that individual business owners, part-time employees and other people in flexible employment can pay voluntary contributions into the housing provident fund and enjoy policy support in accordance with the regulations.
